payload.comment:
The reporting stage is internally consistent and correctly aggregates all pipeline artefacts. All arithmetic cross-checks pass: confusion matrix rows sum to per-class supports (total 7,180), accuracy (6,375/7,180 = 0.887883), macro-F1 (0.855476), macro-precision (0.867173), and macro-recall/balanced-accuracy (0.866479) are all mutually consistent. The abstention report arithmetic is verified (test_coverage = 1 − abstain_rate; selective_risk = 1 − accuracy_on_covered; human_review_count = 7,180 × 0.439276 ≈ 3,154; OOD AUROC = mean of three predictive-entropy test scores = 0.979091). Training history is consistent (best epoch 11, patience 3 → stop at epoch 14; cosine LR schedule values verified). Search report correctly records 4/4 trials completed, test_metrics_used=false, and the selected candidate. Prediction artifact sample counts (7,180 test / 10,004 validation) match the evaluation report. Cross-artifact references (accuracy, sample counts, config hashes) are consistent. No deterministic findings were raised.

However, several substantive concerns warrant a warning-level flag in the final report:

1. Severe validation-to-test generalization gap: val_acc 0.9972 → test_acc 0.8879 (~11 pp drop); val_macro_f1 0.9972 → test_macro_f1 0.8555 (~14 pp drop). The model was selected on validation accuracy (0.982707) which does not reflect test performance, raising questions about the reliability of the selection criterion for this split.

2. Cancer-associated stroma (class 7) has critically low recall (0.508) and F1 (0.647), with 105/421 samples misclassified as debris and 71 as smooth muscle. This is a clinically significant underperformance for a tissue class relevant to cancer assessment.

3. The 43.9% test abstention rate (vs. 20% validation) means nearly half of test predictions are deferred to human review, which is operationally costly and inconsistent with the 80% coverage target set during calibration. The ~24 pp coverage drop from validation to test is a significant deployment reliability concern.

4. OOD evaluation is limited to unit-scale Gaussian noise at three severity levels (scoped as 'controlled_corruption_proxy'); it does not cover semantic OOD shifts (different tissue types, imaging artifacts, domain shift) that may be more relevant in practice.

5. Rationale strings in best_configuration, train_config, and trial configs are truncated (end with '…'), reducing full auditability. The early_stopping_patience change from 1 (search) to 3 (final training) is not explicitly documented as a deliberate escalation in the rationale.

These are model-performance and operational concerns rather than reporting errors. The reporting stage faithfully presents the pipeline results with appropriate anomaly flags. The report should prominently surface the val→test gap, class-7 underperformance, and operational abstention cost to ensure stakeholders have a complete picture before any deployment decision.
